text:
ravi: heads up — spun up sparrow-lite-int4 on staging and ran our short-qa-2k holdout. R@1 collapsed from 0.78 -> 0.63, R@5 ~ unchanged. filing for quick triage. @hana @leo

hana: can you drop the eval artifacts? which index/metric?

ravi: cosine index, artifacts in CI: https://ci.redwood/sparrow/evals/6249999999 (embeddings.npy, recall_summary.json, tsne_viz.png, per_dim_error.csv)

ci-bot: results uploaded: job=6249999999 (sparrow-lite-int4) :file_folder: :white_check_mark:

leo: paste recall_summary.json snippet? curious about mean positives vs nn dist. short queries often sensitive.

ravi: snippet:
```
baseline_fp16_R@1: 0.78
int4_R@1: 0.63
int4_R@5: 0.92
mean_pos_sim: 0.74
mean_nn_sim: 0.76
avg_query_length: 7
```
(weird: mean_nn_sim > mean_pos_sim)

marta: that pattern -> negatives creeping closer. could be asymmetric quant bias or small-dim dominating cosine for short vectors. did you normalize before/after quant?

ravi: we normalized before quant and kept that order for speed. export used symmetric per-channel scale with hard clamp at [-127,127].

hana: pull per_dim_error.csv; any dims with huge relative error or var shift? also check explained variance (PCA) pre/post-quant.

ravi: per-dim CSV top deltas dims [2, 45, 101, 199] rel-error up to 0.55. PCA retained variance dropped: top-10 variance down 12% vs fp16. t-SNE shows tighter central blob + lots of overlap.

leo: run two experiments: (A) asymmetric zero-point export (per-channel) and (B) post-quant per-dim bias correction calibrated on holdout subset. also (C) try L2-normalize after quant instead of before.

marta: also test microbatch change (batch16->batch4) just in case kernel clipping differs on micro-batch path. cheap check.

ravi: kicking runs: job A=6250000001 (asym-int4), B=6250000002 (per-dim-calib), C=6250000003 (l2-after), D=6250000004 (batch4).

ci-bot: job 6250000001 finished: int4-asym -> R@1 0.68, R@5 0.925, mean_pos_sim 0.75, mean_nn_sim 0.75, pca_top10_drop 9%

ci-bot: job 6250000002 finished: per-dim-calib -> R@1 0.77, R@5 0.93, mean_pos_sim 0.76, mean_nn_sim 0.74, pca_top10_drop 3%

ci-bot: job 6250000003 finished: l2-after -> R@1 0.75, R@5 0.93, silhouette 0.27

ci-bot: job 6250000004 finished: batch4 -> R@1 0.64, R@5 0.92 (no change)

leo: per-dim-calib moved R@1 back to near baseline — suggests scale/zero-point mismatch plus a few dims dominating cosine. batch effect seems unrelated (batch4 didn't help).

hana: can we instrument which query examples flip? get a diff list of queries where fp16 NN != int4 NN and examine token lengths/types. short queries under 10 tokens seem over-represented.

ravi: generated diff: ~420 flips, 68% have query length <=9, many are named-entity or numeric-only. attaching sample: `samples_flips.csv` in artifacts.

marta: hypothesis: embedding head has low-energy dims that get noisy after quant and those dims correlate with rare named-entity features. calibration rescales them. let's add a small per-dim multiplier learned on calibration set (simple OLS or scale factor) and bake into export pipeline.

leo: operational asks: (1) add per-dim calibration to model-export (opt-in flag), (2) add CI holdout test: for short-qa-2k, require R@1 >= 0.75 for any new quantized export, (3) add Optimize alert if silhouette drops >0.08 vs baseline.

hana: also add a diagnostic artifact at export time: per-dim rel-error histogram + top-k flip examples. helpful for future triage.

ravi: opened PR: https://git.redwood/inference/sparrow/patches/317 — implements per-dim calibrator, asymmetric export fallback, and adds `--normalize-after-quant` option. notes: calibrator adds ~9ms to cold load and negligible per-request cost.

leo: please run full holdout sweep (short-qa-2k, wiki-short-5k, stack-exchange-1k) with feature flag on before we flip default. also smoke perf for p99 on GPU.

marta: I'll add a unit test in infra-evals: sample 2k short queries, assert mean_pos_sim >= mean_nn_sim OR R@1 >= 0.74.

hana: nice triage. once full sweep passes we can merge behind flag and monitor nightly regressions. thanks team :rocket:

ravi: thanks all — will report back when sweep completes. closing thread for now. :wave:
